===Pronunciation===
{{es-pr|+<audio:LL-Q1321 (spa)-Rodelar-mano.wav>}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|es|:inh|osp:mano|id=hand}}
{{inh+|es|osp|mano}}, from {{inh|es|la|manus}}, from {{inh|es|itc-pro|*manus}}, perhaps from {{der|es|ine-pro|*méh₂r̥|*méh₂-r̥ ~ *mh₂-én-}}, derived from {{der|es|ine-pro|*(s)meh₂-||to beckon}}, or perhaps from {{der|es|ine-pro||*mon-u-}} (see the Proto-Italic entry). Cognate with {{cog|gl|man}} and {{cog|pt|mão}}. Compare {{cog|fr|main}}.

====Noun====
{{es-noun|f}}

# {{lb|es|anatomy|of a person}} [[hand]]
#: {{ux|es|Lávate las '''manos'''.|Wash your '''hands'''.}}
# {{lb|es|of an animal}} front [[foot]]
# {{lb|es|in a game}} [[round]]; [[hand]]
# {{lb|es|of paint}} [[coat]], [[lick]]
# {{lb|es|of a clock}} [[hand]]
# [[skill]], [[talent]]
# {{l|en|mano}} {{gloss|a stone resembling a rolling pin, used to grind maize or other grain on a metate}}
#: {{syn|es|metlapil}}
# A [[group]] of [[people]] united for a [[job]]
#: {{syn|es|grupo}}

=====Usage notes=====
* As with other nouns denoting body parts, the definite article {{m|es|la||the}} is used where English would use a possessive determiner (e.g. {{m|en|my}}, {{m|en|your}}, {{m|en|his}}, or {{m|en|her}}), as long as the verb that it complements is pronominal and therefore implies possession. Examples: "''Lávate las manos, por favor''" (Wash your hands, please) and "''Átale las manos''" (Tie his hands); contrast with "''Dibuja tus manos''" (Draw your hands).
